token.lead: The token proves you look after the machine Yoda is installed on. It appears only in the core container's log.
token.label: Setup token
token.help: You can paste the whole token into the first box; case does not matter. It works once and expires after 24 hours.
token.where1: On the install host, in the folder Yoda is installed in, run:

org.title: Organisation and Yoda's web address
org.lead: The name shows in the side menu, emails and notifications. You can change it later in System settings › General.
org.name: Organisation name (Thai) (required)
org.lineHelp: A short line under the menu, such as the department or hospital name
org.publicUrlHelp: Detected from the address your browser used to open this page. Used in links in email, LINE, Telegram and GitLab, and must match Valid redirect URIs in Keycloak.
org.urlMismatch: You are reaching Yoda at a different address ({origin}) than the one entered. Check it: otherwise the sign-in at the last step returns to the wrong place.
org.urlInvalid: Enter an address like https://portal.example.org (no ? or #)
org.httpWarning: Allowed on an internal network, but passwords and cookies travel unencrypted. Set up an https reverse proxy and use the https address.
org.defaultLocaleHelp: Each person can change their own language.
org.lockedEnv: Set by environment on the install host ({name})
org.proxyHint: Reaching Yoda through a reverse proxy (such as nginx doing https)? Set this in .env and restart, so Yoda sees the proxy's address and https:

admin.title: Create the break-glass admin
admin.lead: A local account for the /recovery page when signing in through Keycloak does not work. It can only see and change the sign-in settings, never anyone's work or data.
admin.hint: Every administrator is told each time this account is used.
admin.codesInKit: The 10 recovery codes go into the recovery kit (step 9) with the master key.
admin.lockedByKit: The recovery kit was downloaded, so this account cannot be replaced during setup. After setup, change its password at /recovery.
admin.passwordHelp: At least 14 characters, not containing the username, and hard to guess (“Good” or better)
admin.totpRequired: Required, because the web address is not this machine (localhost). Scan the QR code with an app such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator, then enter the 6-digit code.
admin.totpRecommended: Recommended, even though the web address is this machine (localhost).

warning.sequence: a run such as abc or 123

check.title: Check the database, file storage and job queue
check.lead: Read-only: nothing is changed. File storage (S3) is set on the install host only.
check.hint: You can always go on; fix anything that failed before going live.
check.failedHint: Something failed: check core's log and the settings on the install host.

signin.title: Connect Keycloak for sign-in
signin.lead: Everyone signs in to Yoda through your organisation's Keycloak (OpenID Connect). The test must pass before the next step.
signin.hint: Save, then press Test. Next opens once the saved values pass.
signin.passed: The saved values passed the test
signin.existingHelp: Recommended: people use the same account as for the hospital's other systems
signin.keycloakValues: Values to put in Keycloak (Clients › yoda-portal)
signin.saveThenTest: This test checks discovery, the JWKS and the client. The real sign-in through Keycloak is the last step.

optional.later: You can skip this and set it later in System settings.
optional.lineVerify: Put this webhook URL in the LINE Developers Console, then press Verify.
optional.backupsHost: The backup container picks up a new backup time or number of days kept within a minute. BACKUP_AT or BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS in the install host's .env override them. The test checks the values.

email.title: Email notifications (SMTP)
email.lead: Used to email notifications to staff and requesters.

line.title: LINE notifications
line.lead: Notifications through your organisation's LINE Official Account.

telegram.title: Telegram notifications
telegram.lead: Enter the bot token, then register the webhook. The webhook secret is generated for you.

more.title: GitLab, AI and backups
more.lead: Connect GitLab, enter the AI provider keys and check backups.

kit.title: Download the recovery kit
kit.lead: One file to recover the system when something goes wrong. Keep it off this machine, and apart from your backups.
kit.contains1: The master key, to decrypt the stored secrets when restoring on a new host
kit.contains2: 10 recovery codes for the break-glass admin (each works once)
kit.contains3: What to do when signing in through Keycloak does not work
kit.once: It can be downloaded once: Yoda never shows the master key again. Store the file as soon as you have it.
kit.lost: If the file is lost: copy the master key from the install host (/var/lib/yoda/core/master-key), and make new recovery codes at /recovery after setup.
kit.stored: I have stored the recovery kit somewhere safe
kit.reissued: A new recovery kit was issued. The recovery codes in the earlier file no longer work: use this one.
kit.reissueHelp: This browser already downloaded the recovery kit. If the file is lost, ask for it again until {at} (the earlier codes then stop working).

claim.title: Sign in through Keycloak to become the first administrator
claim.lead: The person who signs in now becomes the portal's first administrator. From then on everything is done with a Keycloak account.
claim.hint: Use your own Keycloak account, in the IT staff group.
claim.lockHint: Pressing Finish closes setup for good.
claim.how: You go to Keycloak's sign-in page and come back here. The tokens are checked as Yoda will check them, and so is your membership of the staff group.
claim.providerError: Keycloak did not sign you in (cancelled or refused). Check the client's Valid redirect URIs and try again.
claim.adminNeedsTotp: The break-glass admin has no authenticator app, but the web address now needs one. It will be asked to set up TOTP at its first /recovery sign-in; or go back to step 2 and create the account again (possible before the kit is downloaded).

error.invalidToken: The setup token is wrong, expired or already used. Get a new one with yoda-admin setup-token --new.
error.rateLimited: Too many tries. Wait {minutes} min and try again.
error.sessionExpired: The setup session ended. Enter a setup token again (yoda-admin setup-token).
error.weakPassword: The password is too simple. Use at least 14 characters, not repeated, without the username.
error.totpRequired: Set up the authenticator app first: press “Show the QR code”, then enter the 6-digit code.
error.invalidCode: The 6-digit code is wrong. Check the phone's clock and enter a new code.
error.secretsUnavailable: The master key is not usable. Check the master-key file on the install host, then restart core.
error.settingLocked: This value is set on the install host. Change it in .env and restart.
error.invalidSettings: Some values are not valid. Check the fields marked in red.
error.kitDownloaded: The recovery kit was already downloaded. Only the browser that downloaded it can ask again, within 10 minutes.
error.incomplete: Some required steps are not finished.
error.noIssuer: Keycloak is not set up yet. Go back to step 4.
error.noAdmin: The break-glass admin is not created yet. Go back to step 2.
error.provider: Could not reach Keycloak. Check the issuer URL in step 4.
